terms.definition: A microorganism that causes infectious disease: a virus, bacterium, protist or fungus.
terms.examiner: Pathogens infect plants as well as animals.

terms.definition: A disease that can spread from one person or organism to another.
terms.examiner: Spread by air, water or direct contact.

terms.definition: A pathogen that lives and reproduces inside cells, causing cell damage.
A poison made by bacteria that damages tissues and makes us feel ill.
terms.examiner: Salmonella and gonorrhoea are bacterial diseases.

terms.definition: An organism that carries a pathogen from one host to another, such as the mosquito for malaria.
terms.examiner: Controlling vectors is a way to reduce the spread of disease.

terms.definition: A viral disease spread by droplets from sneezes and coughs; fever and a red skin rash.
A virus spread by sexual contact or exchange of body fluids; it attacks the immune system, and untreated can lead to AIDS.
A disease caused by a protist and spread by mosquitoes; recurrent fever.
terms.examiner: Prevented by stopping mosquitoes breeding and using mosquito nets.
